title: Co-marketing creative brief and publisher metadata checklist
summary: Compact creative brief for a co-marketing listing + a technical and metadata acceptance checklist tailored to cloud marketplace publishers (AWS/Azure/GCP). Purpose: streamline copy approvals, ensure technical gating, and reduce back-and-forth between GTM, legal, and engineering.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a single-sheet brief that combines creative direction for a marketplace tile + an actionable metadata and technical acceptance checklist for publishers. Use this when engaging a partner publisher, or when prepping an internal listing for submission to a cloud marketplace. The goal is to reduce iteration by capturing creative constraints, approval owners, and the exact technical gates that block publication.

Audience:
- GTM launch PM and copywriter
- Partner marketing manager
- Marketplace ingestion engineers
- Legal/compliance reviewer

Priority outcomes:
1) One approved headline and 3 short copy variants that work across tile, short description, and social promotion.
2) Clear mapping from Redwood SKUs to publisher SKUs and trial entitlements.
3) A binary technical acceptance checklist (pass/fail) with owners and remediation steps.

Creative brief (tile + listing + social):
- Product name (publisher-facing): Redwood Inference — Hosted API + Dedicated
- Primary positioning sentence (tile headline): "Fast, predictable LLM inference for production apps"
- 1-line short description (30–60 chars): "Low-latency LLM API with enterprise controls"
- 90-word long description (for listing details): "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first inference platform that makes large language models predictable, cost-efficient, and simple to operate. Ship with hosted APIs for rapid prototyping, reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private deployments for regulated workloads. Built-in observability, rollouts, and cost-optimization tools help teams maintain SLAs while lowering per-token cost. Ideal for product teams building chat, summarization, and retrieval-augmented workflows."
- 3 benefit bullets (for tile/listing):
  • Predictable latency and throughput — SLA-backed reserved capacity options
  • Unified interface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
  • Cost-saving controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations
- CTA variants (choose one for tile): "Start free trial", "Request reserved capacity", "Try the API"
- Social blurb (short): "Ship LLM features faster with predictable inference latency and lower per-token costs. Try Redwood Inference on the Marketplace."

Tone and constraints:
- Technical, engineer-friendly language; avoid marketing fluff.
- No claims of "better than" named competitors. Use industry-neutral phrasing.
- Compliance-safe: avoid implying HIPAA/PHI coverage unless Legal signs off for the Private product variant.

Tile image and assets notes:
- Primary image: simple abstract GPU/matrix visual (1920x1080 recommended), must include Redwood logo safe area.
- Secondary screenshots: 
  1) Console trace showing per-route latency 
  2) Cost breakdown by token class
  3) Rollout canary UI
- Alt text for images required (max 125 chars).

Metadata fields publisher will ask for (fill before submission):
- Short title (<= 40 chars): "Redwood Inference API"
- Long title (<= 80 chars): "Redwood Inference — Hosted, Dedicated, and Private LLM Inference"
- Category: AI & Machine Learning / Infrastructure
- Pricing model: usage-based (tokens) + reserved monthly commitments for Dedicated
- Trial type: 14-day API credit + self-serve test keys
- Support contact: gtm-support@redwood.ai
- Data residency options: us-west-2, eu-west-1 (expandable)

Technical acceptance checklist (pass/fail items) — owner in parentheses:
1) SKU mapping completed and verified (Billing) — maps Redwood SKUs to publisher meter names and purchase flows. Include test purchase evidence. (Owner: Billing Ops)
2) Trial entitlement flow implemented (GTM/Eng) — API keys provision 14-day credit, usage caps enforced. (Owner: Product Ops)
3) OAuth/SSO integration for marketplace-managed accounts (if required) — clear redirect URIs and OIDC details documented. (Owner: Integrations Eng)
4) Metering and usage report accessible (Eng/SRE) — daily usage CSV/report endpoint or publisher hooks validated. (Owner: Observability)
5) KMS and secrets handshake documented (Security) — how publisher will encrypt any invoices or customer metadata. (Owner: Security)
6) Compliance blurb vetted (Legal) — listing language for data handling, logging, and retention. (Owner: Legal)
7) Image and asset alt text included (GTM) — assets meet publisher size and accessibility guidelines. (Owner: Design)
8) Localization plan (if submitting to multiple regions) — default en-US copy and any required translations noted. (Owner: GTM Intl)
9) Accessibility checks (contrast, alt text, keyboard nav for screenshots) (Owner: Design/Accessibility)
10) Contact and escalation defined (GTM) — who publisher calls during ingestion failures or content rejections. (Owner: Partner Ops)

Remediation templates (fast responses to publisher feedback):
- If publisher rejects image: provide two alternate images (high contrast + plain background), alt text, and source/attribution.
- If SKU mismatch: escalate to Billing Ops with a mapping table and example purchase transaction id.
- If trial provisioning fails: provide logs from API key service and steps to repro in publisher sandbox.

Localization and i18n guidance:
- Minimum supported locales for launch: en-US, en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR (only on request — default en-US).
- Keep headlines short; translator should preserve tech terms ("inference", "latency", "throughput").
- Flag strings that should not be translated (product names, trademarked phrases).

Accessibility quick checks (publisher gating):
- All images include alt text <=125 chars.
- Contrast ratio for primary tile CTA >=4.5:1.
- Screenshots with UI chrome must have readable font size when scaled to publisher tile preview.

Approval flow and timeline (example for a single marketplace):
- Day 0: Finalize copy and assets (GTM)
- Day 1: Draft submission to publisher ingestion portal (Eng + GTM)
- Day 2–3: Publisher feedback (likely asset sizing or SKU clarifications)
- Day 3–5: Remediation and resubmit (Eng/Billing/Design)
- Day 7: Go-live expected if no regulatory review required

Owner and review matrix:
- Creative sign-off: Product Marketing (Asha Patel)
- Legal sign-off: Legal Counsel (Jordan Lee)
- Technical acceptance: Marketplace Integrations Lead (Miguel Santos)
- Billing acceptance: Billing Ops (Priya Menon)
notes: This is a GTM-facing draft; keep concise and engineer-friendly. Use linked artifacts for canonical Jira/Confluence references. Once copy locks, create a publisher-specific variant (AWS/Azure/GCP) with exact SKU names and meter IDs before submission.
